question: We have learned that the Commission has formally proposed a review of the Birds and Habitats Directives in its 2027 work programme. These directives form the backbone of Europe’s biodiversity conservation toolkit and underpin the Natura 2000 network. This announcement has sparked widespread concern and backlash from more than 2 000 scientists across Europe. The governments of several Member States have also voiced their opposition. 1.
What is the Commission’s view on the severe biodiversity crisis we are currently facing in Europe?
Is it considering dropping its proposal to review these directives and instead bolstering their funding, implementation and effective enforcement?
